name: baseline
title: Four-engine baseline
description: Protected Mesh and the stock Oban, River and Apalis workers. Each engine uses its original producer and default PostgreSQL storage.

name: current
title: Protected Mesh rebuild
description: Current and archived protected Mesh releases alongside stock River and Oban.

name: lean
title: Protected worker and admission
description: Four Mesh builds isolate the smaller fresh-exec worker, set-based claims, and the two changes together. Every job retains a fresh process and two fenced application commits.

name: direct
title: Direct-file producer
description: The compiled Mesh producer reads and decodes the input file after submission. Two stock Mesh controls use the original broker. PostgreSQL uses its default storage for all four engines.

name: storage
title: Large payloads · Mesh storage tuning
description: The two tuned Mesh arms use PostgreSQL EXTERNAL storage for job arguments. The three peers use their default storage. Repeated-character payloads can use substantially more disk with EXTERNAL.

name: symmetric
title: Large payloads · equal storage tuning
description: Every engine stores the full 512 KiB payload with PostgreSQL EXTERNAL storage. Both protected Mesh arms process the same jobs with different producers.

name: ordinary
title: Trusted shared-process handlers · short
description: Ordinary Mesh handlers share a process and credentials and use application-owned PostgreSQL connections. Protected Mesh uses a fresh process and token-fenced writes. All four engines commit both writes independently.

name: ordinary-dense
title: Trusted shared-process handlers · dense
description: Eight runners share 64 slots. Ordinary Mesh handlers run in the application trust domain and make two independently committed writes. The protected control uses a fresh process and a fenced checkout per write.

name: ordinary-slow
title: Trusted shared-process handlers · slow
description: One runner admits up to 64 jobs that each hold for 100 ms between their two application commits. All five arms consume the same 512 submitted jobs.

name: ordinary-sparse
title: Trusted shared-process handlers · sparse
description: One runner and one slot serve 24 singleton arrivals at a five-connection cap, with a 250 ms gap after each settlement.

name: ordinary-large
title: Trusted shared-process handlers · large
description: Every engine stores the 64 submitted 512 KiB arguments with PostgreSQL EXTERNAL storage. The two Mesh arms use the same direct-file producer. Their handlers use either shared-process execution or a fresh process with fenced writes.

name: ordinary-cohort
title: Trusted handlers · grouped successful settlements
description: Both ordinary Mesh arms use the same executable. One uses the original admission and settlement policy. The other claims jobs with a set-based query and can settle up to eight successful jobs in one transaction. Each job still has two independently committed application writes.

name: bulk-slow
title: Trusted slow jobs · set-based enqueue
description: The same ordinary V1 executable switches between the batch and scalar producer. Each 512-job rotation includes the original trusted and protected Mesh builds and all three stock peers.

name: bulk-short
title: Trusted short jobs · batch enqueue and grouped settlements
description: Both Mesh lanes run the same V2 grouped-success scheduler. The producer switches between set-based and scalar enqueue for the identical 128-job submission.

name: persistent
title: Reusable, supervised worker processes
description: The opt-in Mesh worker keeps its process across attempts. The parent owns the PostgreSQL credentials and fences both application calls. The strict Mesh control starts a fresh worker for each attempt.

name: strict-admission
title: Protected set-based admission
description: Compare the original Mesh dispatcher with set-based claim admission on the same host as the peer engines. Both Mesh arms require confirmed claims, fresh workers, two fenced writes, and individual terminal commits.
